::: {.callout-note}
**This page is for the facilitator.** It is rendered with the site but left out of the navbar, so nothing on the site links to it. The track pages under `tracks/` are participant-facing and contain no instructor guidance, which is collected here. The run sheet is the [facilitator guide of the case](eu-frames-guide.qmd).
:::

## The formats

The facilitator chooses the format; participants do not choose, and the home page describes the formats without offering a choice. Each track is an ordered route through pages that already exist on the site, with a docked sidebar of its own (`_sidebar.yml`) and a slides page embedding the deck it runs on. Name the track of a delivery in `delivery.track` of `_variables.yml`, and the callout of the home page links it; the navbar then shows a participant the last track page that they opened. The decisions behind the formats, and the order in which their material is being built, are in `_planning/formats-2026-10-27.md` of the course repository.

| Format | Track | Deck |
|---|---|---|
| One-day workshop | `tracks/eu-frames-one-day/` | `slides/eu-frames-one-day.qmd` |
| Extended course | `tracks/eu-frames-extended/` | the decks of day 1 on the AR4DS site, `slides/eu-frames-one-day.qmd` on day 2, and the decks of day 3 |
| Self-study | `tracks/self-study/` | the full deck, `slides/eu-frames-full.qmd` |

**What the workshop holds.** The three one-day focuses of October 2026 (open science, data tools, methods) were merged into one workshop on 6 November 2026, in four parts: the claim and credibility, with Multi100 and the record of the paper in SCORE; the estimand and the causal graph; the reproduction, with the three reproduced models, few clusters and the slips in the deposits; and robustness, which holds the menu, the class chart with its submissions, the curve of the claim, its inference, a replication and the declared analysis. The tools are taught by the modules of the AR4DS site before the day, and live on the first day of the Extended course. The workshop is taught mainly in the browser lab of the case, with the workspace as an option for those who have installed R. The old addresses of the three focuses and of the three-day course forward to the new pages through `aliases:`.

## The browser lab

The browser lab is a page that runs R in the tab of the browser and holds the five tasks of the exercise beside the workspace. It is live: it loads the data of the case, which are small (a panel of 43 KB), and runs the code of the tasks on them, each fit in a fraction of a second, so the workshop is taught in it. The causal-graph task prints the answers that the pipeline computed with dagitty for the graphs that the cell offers, because dagitty cannot run in the tab; any other graph goes to the workspace.

## The decks

The decks are assembled from the segments in `slides/_segments/eu-frames/`. A deck is a list of `{{< include >}}` lines with its own agenda, aims and part dividers.

**How the optional runs are switched.** In the segment files, every slide of an optional run is marked with `.deepdive` and a `run` attribute (`tools`, `r`, `methods`, `multiverse`). A deck lists the runs that belong to its main flow under `core-runs:` in its YAML, and `slides/core-runs.lua` strips the `.deepdive` mark from those headings, so `nav-tools.html` neither hides them on the `d` key nor badges them as optional. A run that is not listed stays optional: it is hidden in lean mode and has the escape-hatch link on its first slide.

**Why no segment is included twice in one deck.** The segment files contain R chunks with labels, and knitr refuses a duplicate label, so each deck includes each segment at most once.

**Rebuilding a deck.** Edit the segment files for content, or the deck file for order and framing, and render the deck on its own (`quarto render slides/eu-frames-one-day.qmd`). A change to a segment needs every deck that includes it rendered again (`grep -l "eu-frames/_x.qmd" slides/*.qmd`). The project render fails at its final move step on this machine, so decks are rendered one at a time.

## One day

The one-day workshop works on the country-year panel alone, with the methods that it needs, and nothing from the respondent files. In Task 3 participants choose among the analyses that worked on aggregate data; the analyses of KEVF1 and PRL47, which work on respondents, lie outside the day.

**Pages that the formats share.** Every track starts from the [case study](../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd), which tells the original study, SCORE and Multi100, the five reanalysts with an assessment of their choices, and the conversion lesson on how Multi100 turned their statistics into one effect size. The specification menu is taught as the full set of fourteen decisions, on the [decision map](../cases/eu-frames/map.qmd) and the [specification menu](../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd), with the curve of 864 specifications as the subset that an audit judged justifiable for this claim. The helpers of the browser lab and of the workspace refuse an option that is off the curve, with the one-sentence reason recorded in `data/menu_options.csv` and the page that teaches the option. Every result is classed by standard errors clustered by country with the CR2 correction and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; the specification of C6HJR (t = −3.804, r = −0.242) has a CR2 p of 0.0504 on 9.8 degrees of freedom and is not significant under that rule, which is worth saying before anyone asks. The [run sheet of the case](eu-frames-guide.qmd) has the timings of the workshop.

## The Extended course

The Extended course builds two more days around the workshop. Day 1 is the same for every case: credibility and the three Rs, SCORE and Multi100, repositories and data sources, and then R, Positron and Quarto taught live, each session given from its own deck on the AR4DS site. Day 2 is the workshop, unchanged. Day 3 teaches the methods of this case as sessions, panel data, multilevel models with the respondents of the surveys, and Bayesian estimation, and ends with the preregistered specification of each participant turned into a short report written in Quarto and kept under Git. Participants download the Eurobarometer waves from the GESIS archive before the course, and `prep/01_build_respondents.R` in the workspace builds the file of respondents from them. A two-day version drops day 3.

The decks of days 1 and 3 are being written; until they exist, each day page links the modules of its sessions.

## Self-study

The self-study track takes the case through the companion modules in five stages, and a semester course can follow the same route in class. Its pages give the working time of each step and contain their own shortcuts, written to the reader, because no facilitator is there to apply them, and the [run sheet](eu-frames-guide.qmd#run-self-study) repeats the times. What the facilitator can still do for a self-study cohort is keep the live results pipeline running between deliveries, so that a result submitted alone appears on the Multiverse page of the case (`facilitator/live-results-setup.md`).

**The class chart.** The chart on the Multiverse page reads the rows of the shared results Form whose labels have the frozen format of the case, `explore: [tag] <spec>` or `declared: [tag] <spec>`, with no case word after the tag. The labels of the other cases of AR4DS carry the case word, and the chart draws their rows as unclassed diamonds, so clear the Sheet between deliveries of different cases. Each workspace keeps its own tag in `.class-tag`, so ask a cohort to choose one nickname and to pass it as `nickname = "..."` throughout. A chart keeps the rows of earlier deliveries until the sheet is cleared.
